title: Cinderella and the glass slipper.
lines: Once upon a time there was a sweet girl called Cinderella.
She lived in a big house with her stepmother and two stepsisters.
But they were not nice at all.
They were mean and lazy.
Cinderella, scrub the floor!
shouted the stepmother.
Cinderella, wash my dress!
shouted one stepsister.
Cinderella, make my breakfast!
shouted the other.
How annoying!
Cinderella had to work all day long.
She scrubbed, she swept and she cooked.
Scrub, scrub, scrub!
Her clothes turned grey from the ashes in the fireplace.
That's why they called her Cinderella.
But Cinderella always stayed kind.
And she had very sweet little friends.
Do you know who?
The mice!
Little grey mice with pink ears and long tails.
Squeak squeak!
The mice lived in a little hole in the wall.
They helped Cinderella with everything.
They carried threads and buttons, and they made her bed.
Squeak squeak, we'll help you, Cinderella!
And there were also little birds that sang.
Tweet tweet!
One day a letter came from the palace.
The prince was giving a big ball!
All the girls in the land could come and dance.
The stepsisters jumped up and down.
I'm going to dance with the prince!
No, me!
May I come too?
asked Cinderella softly.
The stepmother laughed.
You?
Only if you've done all your work and have a pretty dress!
Cinderella didn't have a pretty dress.
But the mice and the birds got to work.
They sewed and they cut, all day long.
Tap tap tap.
And look: a lovely pink dress!
Cinderella was so happy.
But when the stepsisters saw it, they tore the dress to pieces.
Rrrrip!
Cinderella walked into the garden and started to cry.
Sob, sob.
But then something began to sparkle.
Ping, ping!
A little old lady with a magic wand appeared.
It was her fairy godmother!
Don't cry, dear, said the fairy.
You are going to the ball!
The fairy looked around the garden.
She saw a big, fat, orange pumpkin.
She waved her magic wand and said: Bibbidi-Bobbidi-Boo!
Poof!
The pumpkin grew bigger and bigger, and turned into a beautiful golden coach with wheels!
Wow!
Then she looked at the mice.
Bibbidi-Bobbidi-Boo!
The mice turned into four white horses.
Neigh!
And the horse from the stable became the coachman.
And then Cinderella herself.
Bibbidi-Bobbidi-Boo!
Her torn dress turned into a sparkling blue ball gown.
And on her feet she wore two glass slippers, shoes that sparkled like little stars.
But remember one thing, said the fairy.
At twelve o'clock at night the magic ends.
Then everything goes back to how it was.
The golden coach drove to the palace.
Clip-clop, clip-clop.
When Cinderella came in, everyone looked.
Who is that pretty girl?
The prince saw her and asked: Will you dance with me?
They danced and danced, all evening long.
It was such fun!
But suddenly: Bong!
The clock began to strike.
Bong!
Bong!
It was twelve o'clock!
Oh no, I have to go!
cried Cinderella.
She ran down the big stairs of the palace.
Tap tap tap.
And on the stairs she lost one of her glass slippers!
But she had no time to pick it up.
Bong!
Poof!
The coach became a pumpkin again, and the horses became mice again.
Squeak squeak!
The next day the prince looked everywhere for the girl with the glass slipper.
Every girl had to try it on.
The stepsisters pushed and pulled, but their feet were much too big.
Ow ow ow!
Then Cinderella was allowed to try it on.
And what do you think?
The slipper fit perfectly!
The prince was so happy.
Cinderella married the prince, and the mice came along to the palace too.
Squeak squeak, hooray!
